cues.en: Somewhat annoyingly, there are different notations that are used for the derivative or the process of differentiation.
cues.zh: 有點惱人的是，導數或微分過程，有不同的記號。

cues.en: Well, okay, it's not really annoying per se.
cues.zh: 好吧，本身其實不算惱人。

cues.en: Different notations can be useful in different situations, but the different notations can be a little bit confusing at first.
cues.zh: 不同記號在不同情況可能很好用，只是一開始可能有點混淆。

cues.en: And so I made this video just to introduce you to the different notations that you will see for the
cues.zh: 所以我做了這支影片，介紹你會看到的不同記號，它們代表

cues.en: exact same mathematical operation of differentiation, not only in this course, but everywhere else where you see calculus.
cues.zh: 完全相同的微分運算。不只在這門課，任何出現微積分的地方都會看到。

cues.en: And then towards the end of the video, I will also clarify some geometric terms and explain how those are related to differentiation.
cues.zh: 影片後段，我也會釐清一些幾何術語，解釋它們和微分的關係。

cues.en: So there are four common derivative notations that you will see, and they are given to us by different mathematicians.
cues.zh: 你會看到四種常見的導數記號，它們來自不同數學家。

cues.en: So these guys are the namesakes of the notations.
cues.zh: 這些記號都是以他們的名字命名。

cues.en: I'll go through each one in turn.
cues.zh: 我會依序說明。

cues.en: Let's start with Leibniz.
cues.zh: 先從萊布尼茲開始。

cues.en: Leibniz notation looks like this.
cues.zh: 萊布尼茲記號長這樣。

cues.en: In fact, you've already seen this notation before.
cues.zh: 其實你已經看過。

cues.en: This is the notation that you usually start off with when learning calculus, because it really shows how the derivative is conceptually similar to the slope of a line.
cues.zh: 學微積分時，通常從這個記號開始，因為它很清楚地呈現，導數在概念上和直線斜率很像。

cues.en: So these different terms here are all equivalent.
cues.zh: 所以這裡的不同寫法，都等價。

cues.en: They're all the same thing, just slight variations on the same idea.
cues.zh: 都是一樣的東西，只是相同想法的小變化。

cues.en: So here we have d, y by d x, here we have df by d x, so indicating the change in the function.
cues.zh: 這裡有 dy/dx，這裡有 df/dx，表示函數的變化。

cues.en: And sometimes the F is also written outside of the fraction.
cues.zh: 有時 f 也會寫在分數外面。

cues.en: So we would have D by x of f of x.
cues.zh: 所以會寫成 d/dx，作用在 f(x) 上。

cues.en: Anyway, these are all the same thing.
cues.zh: 總之，這些都一樣。

cues.en: Here is the notation for the second derivative.
cues.zh: 這是二階導數的記號。

cues.en: Now, I haven't yet talked about higher order derivatives.
cues.zh: 我還沒談過高階導數。

cues.en: That's coming up later in the course, but essentially it's just the derivative of the derivative and higher derivatives.
cues.zh: 課程後面會談，基本上就是導數的導數。高階導數，

cues.en: Tell you about the changes in the derivative.
cues.zh: 告訴你導數的變化。

cues.en: So how the derivative itself is changing.
cues.zh: 也就是導數本身如何改變。

cues.en: So we'll come back to this later.
cues.zh: 所以之後會再回來談。

cues.en: Initially, it looks like the second derivative seems a little weird because the x is squared here, but the dx is squared in the numerator.
cues.zh: 一開始，二階導數看起來有點怪，這裡 x 是平方，而分子裡 d 是平方。

cues.en: That will actually make sense later in the course when I teach you about higher order derivatives.
cues.zh: 之後教高階導數時，這就會變得合理。

cues.en: So Leibniz notation, it's really common because it's clear and it's easy to understand.
cues.zh: 所以萊布尼茲記號很常見，因為清楚，也容易理解。

cues.en: It also facilitates understanding the chain rule which can be broken down like this.
cues.zh: 它也有助於理解鏈鎖律，可以像這樣拆開。

cues.en: Now, don't worry about what this means or where this u comes from.
cues.zh: 先不用擔心意思，或這個 u 從哪裡來。

cues.en: You'll learn all about the chain rule in a later video.
cues.zh: 之後的影片會完整介紹鏈鎖律。

cues.en: I just wanted to show you the notation here.
cues.zh: 我只是想先展示記號。

cues.en: I don't know if there are really any disadvantages to loudness notation per se, but it does take up a little bit more space and it's a little longer to write out.
cues.zh: 我不知道萊布尼茲記號本身有什麼缺點，但它確實稍微占空間，寫起來也比較長。

cues.en: So I don't know, maybe that's that's a disadvantage.
cues.zh: 所以也許那算是缺點。

cues.en: Anyway, you generally start writing out derivatives like this, and then once you get more comfortable
cues.zh: 總之，通常一開始會這樣寫導數，等你更熟悉

cues.en: with the concept and use of derivatives, you switch to a more efficient and compact notation.
cues.zh: 導數的概念與使用，就會改用更有效率、更簡潔的記號。

cues.en: And that brings me to the Lagrangian notation.
cues.zh: 這就帶到拉格朗日記號。

cues.en: This one is nice and compact.
cues.zh: 這個很簡潔。

cues.en: It's used very often.
cues.zh: 很常使用。

cues.en: You simply put an apostrophe after the F or whatever is the letter used to indicate the function.
cues.zh: 只要在 f，或任何用來表示函數的字母後面，加上撇號。

cues.en: This we call Prime.
cues.zh: 我們叫它 prime。

cues.en: So you would pronounce this as f prime of x or the derivative of x.
cues.zh: 所以會唸成 f prime of x，或 x 的函數之導數。

cues.en: And yeah, also some slight variations of Lagrange notation.
cues.zh: 拉格朗日記號也有些小變化。

cues.en: Here is what the second derivative looks like.
cues.zh: 這是二階導數的樣子。

cues.en: Again, super simple, clean and easy to write out and you don't need to worry about fractions and writing these smaller letters and so on.
cues.zh: 同樣很簡單、清楚、好寫，不需要煩惱分數，或寫這些小字母等等。

cues.en: And this notation is also convenient for indicating partial derivatives.
cues.zh: 這個記號，也很方便表示偏導數。

cues.en: Partial derivatives are when you have more than one independent variable.
cues.zh: 當你有不只一個自變數時，就會有偏導數。

cues.en: And so then you hold one variable constant while computing the variable of computing the derivative of the other variable.
cues.zh: 這時固定其中一個變數，再計算另一個變數的導數。

cues.en: You'll learn more about that in the section on multivariate calculus.
cues.zh: 多變數微積分單元，會再詳細學。

cues.en: And I don't know if there are any real disadvantages of the Lagrange notation.
cues.zh: 我也不知道拉格朗日記號有什麼真正的缺點。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And then we have the Newton notation.
cues.zh: 接著是牛頓記號。

cues.en: This one is also simple and elegant.
cues.zh: 這也簡單優雅。

cues.en: You just put a dot on top of the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 只需要在依變數上方加點。

cues.en: So this is the derivative of Y and this is the second derivative of Y and so on.
cues.zh: 所以這是 y 的導數，這是 y 的二階導數，依此類推。

cues.en: This one is also compact, although on most keyboards you need a special character to insert as opposed to the Lagrange notation where every keyboard has an apostrophe key.
cues.zh: 它也很簡潔，不過大多數鍵盤需要插入特殊字元，不像拉格朗日記號，每個鍵盤都有撇號鍵。

cues.en: So for that reason alone, this is slightly less commonly used, but Newton notation is mainly used to indicate the derivative of something.
cues.zh: 光是這個原因，它就稍微少用一些。不過牛頓記號主要用來表示某個量

cues.en: Over time, typically a physical force.
cues.zh: 對時間的導數，通常是物理作用力。

cues.en: So if you're going into physics, if you're studying physics, then you will see this notation quite a bit.
cues.zh: 所以如果你要進入物理領域、正在學物理，就會經常看到這個記號。

cues.en: Outside of that context, you might not see it that often.
cues.zh: 在這以外，可能不常看到。

cues.en: I guess the disadvantage of Newton's notation is that it's not used for partial derivatives.
cues.zh: 我想，牛頓記號的缺點，是不用來表示偏導數。

cues.en: So for partial derivatives, you would switch back to some other form of notation.
cues.zh: 所以遇到偏導數，會換回其他形式的記號。

cues.en: And then we have the Euler notation.
cues.zh: 接著是歐拉記號。

cues.en: Pretty simple.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: It's just a capital D in front of the function variable.
cues.zh: 就是在函數變數前面放大寫 D。

cues.en: And then the second derivative is indicated with a superscript.
cues.zh: 二階導數則用上標表示。

cues.en: And yeah, this is also a very simple and compact notation, but it is the least commonly used.
cues.zh: 這也是非常簡單、簡潔的記號，不過最少使用。

cues.en: And in part that's because it can be confused with the domain of a function and also in part because it also doesn't lend itself very well to indicating partial derivatives.
cues.zh: 一部分是因為可能和函數的定義域混淆，一部分也是因為它不太方便表示偏導數。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So here you see the summary of all of these different notations.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到所有不同記號的整理。

cues.en: These two are the most common.
cues.zh: 這兩種最常見。

cues.en: This one is more common in physics when describing forces over time or the derivative of something over time.
cues.zh: 這種在物理比較常見，用來描述隨時間的作用力，或某個量對時間的導數。

cues.en: This one is good to know about, but I don't think you're really going to see it that much.
cues.zh: 這種知道就好，我想你不會太常看到。

cues.en: Certainly not for the rest of this course.
cues.zh: 至少這門課後面不會。

cues.en: Okay, On to a bit of geometry.
cues.zh: 好，進入一點幾何。

cues.en: Now, there are two terms that you need to understand and let me take a moment to clarify them.
cues.zh: 有兩個術語需要理解，我花點時間釐清。

cues.en: Secant lines and tangent lines.
cues.zh: 割線與切線。

cues.en: These are both descriptions of straight lines that pass through functions.
cues.zh: 兩者都是對穿過函數圖形之直線的描述。

cues.en: Now, the common definition that you often hear is that a secant line passes through two points, whereas a tangent line passes through one point.
cues.zh: 常聽到的定義，是割線通過兩點，而切線通過一點。

cues.en: But well, let's start with an example.
cues.zh: 不過，先看個例子。

cues.en: Here is an example of a secant line.
cues.zh: 這裡是一條割線。

cues.en: It passes through this function x squared and it touches exactly two points.
cues.zh: 它穿過 x 平方這個函數，恰好碰到兩個點。

cues.en: And here is a tangent line.
cues.zh: 這裡是一條切線。

cues.en: Now, you can already imagine that as these two points here get closer and closer together, the second line is going to turn into the tangent line.
cues.zh: 你已經可以想像，當這兩個點越來越接近，割線就會變成切線。

cues.en: But, you know, these definitions are not really precise.
cues.zh: 不過，這些定義其實不太精確。

cues.en: For example, this line passes through the function at one point, but it's definitely not a tangent line.
cues.zh: 例如，這條線穿過函數的一個點，但絕對不是切線。

cues.en: And I don't know, maybe this really is a secant line because it's going to pass through this function somewhere up here, maybe off the screen.
cues.zh: 我也不知道，也許它其實是割線，因為還會在上面某處、螢幕外穿過函數。

cues.en: But, you know, actually this line here, this truly is a tangent line and it passes through this function one, two, three, four times at least.
cues.zh: 不過這裡這條，確實是切線，卻穿過函數一、二、三、四，至少四次。

cues.en: And who knows, maybe more times.
cues.zh: 誰知道，也許還有更多次。

cues.en: I don't know what happens over here.
cues.zh: 我不知道這邊會怎樣。

cues.en: Maybe it's a piecewise function and it comes up.
cues.zh: 也許是分段函數，之後又往上。

cues.en: So here is a more accurate definition of a tangent line.
cues.zh: 所以，這是更精確的切線定義。

cues.en: A tangent line passes through two points, but those two points are like an infinitesimal distance apart.
cues.zh: 切線通過兩個點，但它們之間相隔無窮小的距離。

cues.en: So there's so close that you can kind of almost think of them as a single point, but they technically are two separate points.
cues.zh: 靠得如此接近，幾乎可以當成一個點，但嚴格來說，仍是兩個不同點。

cues.en: And that leads me to the geometric interpretation or really the definition of the derivative.
cues.zh: 這就帶到導數的幾何解讀，或者說定義。

cues.en: So the derivative in geometry, geometric terms is the slope of the tangent line.
cues.zh: 幾何上，導數就是切線的斜率。

cues.en: At some point X on a function F of x, and that tangent line is defined as the line that passes through two points.
cues.zh: 是函數 f(x) 在某個 x 點的切線斜率，而切線定義成通過兩個點的直線，

cues.en: But those points are an infinitesimal distance apart on the x axis.
cues.zh: 但兩點在 x 軸上相隔無窮小的距離。

cues.en: And by the way, you know from the video on this term, infinitesimal, it's where is the end of the limit section that I'm using this term kind of colloquially here.
cues.zh: 順便說，從極限單元結尾談無窮小的影片，你知道我這裡是用比較口語的意思。

cues.en: You can also say that the tangent line is what you get when you take a second line and you bring Delta X smaller and smaller as the limit approach is zero.
cues.zh: 也可以說，取一條割線，讓 Δx 越來越小，取趨近零時的極限，就得到切線。

cues.en: I hope you enjoyed this video.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡這支影片。

cues.en: The main take home is that there are several different notations for indicating differentiation and some circumstances where certain notations are preferred over others.
cues.zh: 主要重點是，有好幾種表示微分的記號，在某些情況會偏好某些記號。

cues.en: But in many cases which notation you use or you see is just a matter of personal preference.
cues.zh: 但很多時候，用哪個、看到哪個，只是個人偏好。
